# Press Release


## SOUTHERN MISSOURI BANCORP REPORTS PRELIMINARY RESULTS FOR FIRST QUARTER OF FISCAL 2027; DECLARES QUARTERLY DIVIDEND OF $0.27 PER COMMON SHARE; CONFERENCE CALL SCHEDULED FOR THURSDAY, OCTOBER 22, AT 9:30 AM CENTRAL TIME


Company Release - 10/21/2026


[Download the PDF version PDF Format (opens in new window) PDF 1.06 MB](https://s1.q4cdn.com/643710937/files/content_files/SMBC-8K-Earnings-Release-09-30-2026.pdf)


Poplar Bluff, Missouri, Oct. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Southern Missouri Bancorp, Inc. (“Company”) (NASDAQ: SMBC), the parent corporation of Southern Bank (“Bank”), today announced preliminary net income for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 of $19.1 million, an increase of $3.4 million, or 22.0%, as compared to the same period of the prior fiscal year. The increase was driven by higher net interest income, lower provision for credit losses (PCL), and higher noninterest income. This was partially offset by higher noninterest expense and higher provision for income taxes. Preliminary net income was $1.73 per fully diluted common share for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, an increase of $0.35, or 25.4%, as compared to $1.38 per fully diluted common share reported for the same period of the prior fiscal year.


**Highlights for the first quarter of fiscal 2027:**


- Earnings per common share (diluted) were $1.73, up $0.35, or 25.4%, as compared to the same quarter a year ago, and down $0.10, or 5.5%, from the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the linked quarter. During the year-ago quarter, the Company incurred $572,000 of non-recurring consulting expenses related to renegotiation of a significant bank contract, reducing after-tax net income by $444,000, or $0.04 per fully diluted common share, with no similar charges in the current quarter.


- Annualized return on average assets (ROA) was 1.44%, while annualized return on average common equity (ROE) was 12.7%, as compared to 1.24% and 11.3%, respectively, in the same quarter a year ago, and 1.57% and 14.0%, respectively, in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the linked quarter.


- Net interest margin for the quarter was 3.70%, up from 3.57% reported for the year-ago period, and up from 3.67% reported for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the linked quarter. Net interest income increased $3.5 million, or 8.3%, as compared to the same quarter a year ago, and increased $1.5 million, or 3.5%, as compared to the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the linked quarter.


- PCL was $3.0 million during the first quarter of fiscal 2027, a decrease of $1.5 million from the year-ago period and a decrease of $240,000 from the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the linked quarter.


- Provision for income taxes was $4.5 million, an increase of $678,000 from the prior-year quarter and an increase of $1.7 million from the linked quarter, primarily reflecting a $1.7 million tax benefit from tax credit investments recognized in the linked quarter that did not recur.


- Gross loan balances increased by $63.9 million during the first quarter of fiscal 2027, or 1.5%, and increased by $263.9 million, or 6.3%, over the last twelve months.


- Deposit balances increased by $66.1 million during the first quarter of fiscal 2027, or 1.5%, and increased by $193.5 million, or 4.5%, over the last twelve months.


- Tangible book value per share was $48.52 as of September 30, 2026, and increased by $5.17, or 11.9%, during the last twelve months.


- The Company repurchased 19,000 shares of its common stock in the first quarter of 2027 at an average price of $72.63 per share, for a total of $1.4 million. The average purchase price was 150% of our tangible book value as of September 30, 2026.


**Dividend Declared:**


The Board of Directors, on October 20, 2026, declared a quarterly cash dividend on common stock of $0.27, payable November 30, 2026, to stockholders of record at the close of business on November 13, 2026, marking the 130th consecutive quarterly dividend since the inception of the Company. The Board of Directors and management believe the payment of a quarterly cash dividend enhances stockholder value and demonstrates our commitment to and confidence in our future prospects.


**Conference Call:**


The Company will host a conference call to review the information provided in this press release on Thursday, October 22, 2026, at 9:30 a.m., Central Time. The call will be available live to interested parties by calling 1-833-461-5787 in the United States and from all other locations by calling 1-585-542-9983. Participants should use participant access code 953340433. Telephone playback will be available beginning one hour following the conclusion of the call through October 27, 2026. The playback may be accessed by dialing 1-833-309-1852 in the United States and Canada, and using the conference passcode 953340433.


**Balance Sheet Summary:**


The Company experienced balance sheet growth during the first quarter of fiscal 2027, with total assets of $5.3 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $74.4 million, or 1.4%, compared to June 30, 2026. Growth was driven primarily by increases in net loans receivable, other assets, cash equivalents and time deposits, and available-for-sale (AFS) securities. The increase in other assets was primarily driven by an increase in accrued interest receivable.


Cash equivalents and time deposits were $97.1 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of $6.2 million, or 6.8%, compared to June 30, 2026. AFS securities were $454.1 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of $3.3 million, or 0.7%, compared to June 30, 2026.


Loans, net of the allowance for credit losses (ACL), were $4.4 billion at September 30, 2026, increasing by $60.5 million, or 1.4%, compared to June 30, 2026. Gross loans increased by $63.9 million, or 1.5%, to $4.5 billion, while the ACL increased by $3.4 million, compared to June 30, 2026. The Company noted growth primarily in loans collateralized by 1-4 family residential real estate, agriculture production, commercial and industrial, agriculture real estate, and construction and land development. This was partially offset by decreases in loans collateralized by multi-family real estate, non-owner occupied commercial real estate, and owner occupied commercial real estate. Loans anticipated to fund in the next 90 days totaled $184.8 million at September 30, 2026, as compared to $181.7 million at June 30, 2026, and $194.5 million at September 30, 2025.


The Bank’s concentration in non-owner occupied commercial real estate loans, as defined by banking regulatory guidance and including multi-family and construction and land development loans, is estimated at 277.7% of Tier 1 capital and ACL at September 30, 2026, as compared to 287.7% as of June 30, 2026, the linked quarter end, with these loans representing 37.9% of total loans at September 30, 2026. The largest component of this concentration is non-owner occupied commercial real estate, which is primarily comprised of loans secured by hospitality (hotels and restaurants), care facilities, strip centers, retail stand-alone properties, and storage units. Within this portfolio, the hospitality and retail stand-alone segments consist primarily of franchised businesses; care facilities consist mainly of skilled nursing and assisted living centers; and strip centers are generally non-mall shopping centers with a variety of tenants. The Bank’s multi-family real estate loan portfolio includes loans secured by properties currently participating in the low-income housing tax credit (LIHTC) program or that have exited the program. The largest component of the construction and land development portfolio is commercial construction, consisting primarily of loans collateralized by multi-family real estate and industrial warehouse developments. The Company continues to monitor its commercial real estate concentration and each of its individual segments closely.


Nonperforming loans (NPLs) were $26.7 million, or 0.60% of gross loans, at September 30, 2026, compared to $27.7 million, or 0.63% of gross loans, at June 30, 2026, a decrease of $996,000, or 3.6%. Nonperforming assets (NPAs) were $32.4 million, or 0.61% of total assets, at September 30, 2026, compared to $33.5 million, or 0.64% of total assets, at June 30, 2026, a decrease of $1.1 million, or 3.3%, primarily due to lower NPLs. Performing loan modifications to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty totaled $51.1 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $31.0 million at June 30, 2026. The increase was primarily attributable to the modification of payment terms on a commercial and industrial loan.


The ACL totaled $58.3 million at September 30, 2026, representing 1.31% of gross loans and 218.6% of nonperforming loans, compared to $54.9 million, or 1.25% of gross loans and 198.6% of nonperforming loans, at June 30, 2026. The Company has estimated its expected credit losses as of September 30, 2026, under ASC 326-20, and management believes the ACL as of that date was adequate based on that estimate. Economic uncertainty remains, including the potential effects of elevated and uncertain interest rates, as inflation remains above the Federal Reserve's long-term target, and evolving labor market and broader economic conditions. The increase in the ACL was primarily attributable to management’s assessment of reserve adequacy amid the economic uncertainty and to support loan growth. This was partially offset by net charge-offs of $494,000 in the three-month period ended September 30, 2026. As a percentage of average loans outstanding, the Company recorded net charge offs of 0.04% (annualized) during the current quarter, as compared to 0.36% for the same quarter of the prior fiscal year, and 0.40% during the linked quarter.


Total liabilities were $4.7 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $63.9 million, or 1.4%, compared to June 30, 2026. Increases in total deposits and securities sold under agreements to repurchase were partially offset by a reduction in FHLB advances.


Deposits were $4.5 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $66.1 million, or 1.5%, compared to June 30, 2026. Certificate of deposit growth was primarily driven by non-brokered certificates of deposit and was partially offset by a decrease in brokered certificates of deposit. Nonmaturity deposit growth was primarily attributable to increases in non-brokered and brokered money market deposit accounts. This was partially offset by declines in non-interest bearing deposits, NOW accounts, and savings accounts. Public unit balances totaled $475.4 million at September 30, 2026, a decrease of $42.4 million compared to June 30, 2026, primarily due to competitive pricing dynamics on certain time deposits and normal fluctuations in operating account balances. Brokered deposits totaled $271.4 million at September 30, 2026, a decrease of $19.3 million as compared to June 30, 2026, attributable to a decrease in brokered certificates of deposit, which was partially offset by an increase in brokered money market deposit accounts. The average loan-to-deposit ratio for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 was 98.8%, as compared to 99.7% for the linked quarter, and 96.3% for the same period of the prior fiscal year. FHLB advances were $122.7 million at September 30, 2026, a decrease of $7.7 million, or 5.9%, from June 30, 2026. Outstanding FHLB daily reset borrowings were $27.7 million as of September 30, 2026, as compared to $28.4 million outstanding as of June 30, 2026.


The Company’s stockholders’ equity was $601.1 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of $10.5 million, or 1.8%, compared to June 30, 2026. The increase was attributable primarily to earnings retained after cash dividends paid. This increase was partially offset by a $4.7 million increase in accumulated other comprehensive loss (AOCL), as the market value of the Company’s investments declined due to higher market interest rates, and $1.4 million used to repurchase 19,000 shares of the Company’s common stock during the first quarter of fiscal 2027 at an average price of $72.63 per share. AOCL totaled $14.4 million at September 30, 2026, as compared to $9.8 million at June 30, 2026. The Company does not hold any securities classified as held-to-maturity.


**Quarterly Income Statement Summary:**


The Company’s net interest income for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, was $45.9 million, an increase of $3.5 million, or 8.3%, as compared to the same period of the prior fiscal year. The increase reflected a 4.5% increase in the average balance of interest-earning assets and a 13-basis point increase in net interest margin, from 3.57% to 3.70%. The primary driver of the net interest margin expansion, compared to the year ago period, was a decrease in the cost of interest-bearing liabilities of 19 basis points, partially offset by a decrease of four basis points in the yield on interest-earning assets.


Loan discount accretion and liability premium amortization related to the November 2018 acquisition of First Commercial Bank, the May 2020 acquisition of Central Federal Savings & Loan Association, the February 2022 merger of FortuneBank, and the January 2023 acquisition of Citizens Bank & Trust resulted in $682,000 in net interest income for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $876,000 in net interest income for the same period a year ago. Combined, this component of net interest income contributed approximately five basis points to net interest margin in the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, as compared to approximately seven basis points for the same period of the prior fiscal year and approximately three basis points in the linked quarter ended June 30, 2026, when net interest margin was 3.67%.


The Company recorded a PCL of $3.0 million in the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, as compared to a PCL of $4.5 million in the same period of the prior fiscal year. The current period PCL was the result of a $3.9 million provision attributable to the ACL for outstanding loan balances and a $902,000 negative provision attributable to the allowance for off-balance sheet credit exposures, primarily reflecting a lower required reserve rate on unfunded commitments. The allowance for off-balance-sheet credit exposures, included in other liabilities, totaled $3.5 million at September 30, 2026. The factors considered when estimating the required ACL and PCL for loan balances outstanding are detailed above in the “Balance Sheet Summary.”


The Company’s noninterest income for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, was $7.1 million, an increase of $573,000, or 8.7%, as compared to the same period of the prior fiscal year. The increase was primarily driven by higher other noninterest income, reflecting increased merchant program income and the gain on sale of membership interest in a tax credit investment, and higher deposit account charges and related fees, driven by a higher volume of nonsufficient funds charges. Noninterest income also benefited from increased earnings on bank-owned life insurance, including a $150,000 mortality benefit recognized in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, and higher bank card interchange income. These increases were partially offset by lower other loan fees, as swap fees were recognized in the prior-year period but not in the current period.


Noninterest expense for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, was $26.6 million, an increase of $1.5 million, or 6.1%, as compared to the same period of the prior fiscal year. The increase was driven primarily by an increase in compensation and benefits expense, reflecting annual merit increases, higher team member headcount, and lower compensation costs deferred related to loan originations. In addition, other noninterest expense increased primarily due to higher costs associated with deposit operations and card fraud, as well as loan collection and other lending-related activities. Occupancy and equipment expense increased due to equipment purchases, maintenance and repairs, and insurance costs, while data processing expense increased as a result of higher software, digital banking, and information security-related costs. These increases were partially offset by lower legal and professional fees, as the prior-year period included $572,000 of consulting costs associated with the negotiation of a new contract with a key vendor, with no similar activity in the current quarter, and lower intangible amortization expense following the full amortization of a core deposit intangible in the second quarter of fiscal 2026.


The efficiency ratio for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, was 50.0%, as compared to 51.1% in the same period of the prior fiscal year. The improvement was driven by the increase in net interest income and noninterest income, which more than offset the increase in noninterest expense.


The income tax provision for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, was $4.5 million, an increase of $678,000, or 17.9%, as compared to the same period of the prior fiscal year, primarily due to the increase in net income before income taxes. The effective tax rate for the quarter was 19.0%, compared to 19.5% in the same quarter of the prior fiscal year.

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures:**


Tangible common equity and tangible book value per common share are financial measures determined by methods other than in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (GAAP). These non-GAAP financial measures are supplemental and are not intended to be a substitute for analyses based on GAAP measures. As other companies may utilize different methodologies for calculating these measures, this presentation may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other institutions.


Tangible common equity is calculated by excluding intangible assets from common stockholders’ equity. Tangible book value per common share is calculated by dividing tangible common equity by common shares outstanding, less restricted common shares not vested. For comparison, book value per common share is calculated by dividing common stockholders’ equity by common shares outstanding, less restricted common shares not vested. This approach is consistent with the treatment applied by bank regulatory agencies, which generally exclude intangible assets from the calculation of risk-based capital ratios.


Each of these non-GAAP financial measures provides information considered important to investors and is useful in understanding the Company’s capital position.
